text:
Title: What is HisabDo?

HisabDo is a bookkeeping and expense-management app that helps small businesses and individuals track expenses, income, and cash flow, and get an AI-assisted breakdown of where their money is going.
title: What is HisabDo?

text:
Title: How do I categorize an expense? How does automatic expense categorization work?

When you add an expense, HisabDo predicts a category using a combination of rule-based matching and a machine learning model trained on past expense descriptions. If the model isn't confident, the expense is flagged for you to confirm or correct the category instead of being applied automatically.
title: How do I categorize an expense? How does automatic expense categorization work?

text:
Title: Is my financial data used to train the shared AI model?

No individual user's raw financial data is used as a knowledge source for the chatbot. Chatbot answers about your own balance, expenses, or revenue are always pulled live from your account through the backend, not from any shared knowledge base.
title: Is my financial data used to train the shared AI model?

text:
Title: What is a cash flow statement?

A cash flow statement is a financial report that shows the money moving in and out of a business over a period of time, split into operating, investing, and financing activities. It helps you see whether a business is generating enough cash to sustain itself.
title: What is a cash flow statement?

text:
Title: How do I export my expenses or get my spending data?

To export your recorded expenses or get your spending data out of HisabDo, open the Reports section and export a CSV or PDF report. You can filter the report by date range, category, or tag.
title: How do I export my expenses or get my spending data?

text:
Title: What's the difference between profit and cash flow?

Profit is revenue minus expenses over a period, based on accounting rules, while cash flow is the actual movement of money in and out of your accounts. A business can be profitable on paper while still running low on cash if customers haven't paid yet.
title: What's the difference between profit and cash flow?

text: Title: What is profit? Profit is the amount remaining after expenses are subtracted from revenue.
title: What is profit?

text: Title: What is revenue? Revenue is the total income generated from business sales or services before expenses are deducted.
title: What is revenue?

text: Title: What is an expense? An expense is a cost incurred by a business while operating or generating revenue.
title: What is an expense?

text: Title: What is cash flow? Cash flow represents the movement of money entering and leaving a business during a period.
title: What is cash flow?

text: Title: Why should customer balances be tracked? Tracking customer balances helps a business identify outstanding payments and monitor money owed by customers.
title: Why should customer balances be tracked?

text: Title: Why should business expenses be categorized? Categorizing expenses makes financial records easier to analyze and helps identify where business money is being spent.
title: Why should business expenses be categorized?

text: Title: What is a balance sheet? A balance sheet summarizes a business's assets, liabilities, and owner's equity at a specific point in time.
title: What is a balance sheet?

text: Title: What are accounts payable and accounts receivable? Accounts payable is money a business owes to suppliers. Accounts receivable is money customers owe to the business.
title: What are accounts payable and accounts receivable?

text: Title: What is a budget? A budget estimates income and expenses over a future period and helps compare planned results with actual results.
title: What is a budget?

text: Title: What is the break-even point? The break-even point is where total revenue equals total costs, resulting in neither profit nor loss.
title: What is the break-even point?
